title: Tie runs are sorted by deeper keys before the merge sort
body:
The sort phase in `construct` sorts each partition by its 64-bit key and hands every run of equal keys to `merge_sort`, which compares suffixes from the first character. Suffixes in a run share the key's characters, 21 for DNA, so every comparison in the run re-reads them.

## Proposal

A `sort_run` that encodes a second key at `start + depth` for each suffix of a run, sorts the run by it, reads the LCP between unequal keys as `depth + shared`, and recurses into the ties with the depth grown by the key's characters, handing a run to `merge_sort` only under a mask, past the cap, or past a fixed depth. `merge_sort` and `merge` take a floor, the characters the run is known to share, and `find_lcp` starts past it.

## Rejected

Measured on 2026-11-05 with the floor at 128 characters, 10 MiB fixtures, 4 threads, median of 5, against 8a05eb2: normal 1.03x, protein 1.08x, long-n 1.41x with peak memory 85 to 218 MiB, long-repeats 1.49x. Each level allocates a key per suffix of the run and the recursion holds every level's keys alive, which is the memory on long-n, whose runs of N are one giant tie run. On long-repeats every suffix sits in a run of ten copies, and six levels of keys per run cost more than the merge sort, whose LCP cache answers those comparisons at once. The patch is `tmp-claude/2026-11-05-construct-refactor/floor-and-deeper.patch`.

## Open

Whether a size threshold, deeper keys only for runs over some length, keeps the win on the capped case without the loss on repeats. Not tried.
